object.content:
Last night I decided to fix my girlfriend's broken Keurig B70 coffee maker. It wouldn't turn on so I used a disassembly guide (http://www.singleservecoffeeforums.com/dissassembly-repair-guide-keurig-b70-platinum-t8124.html) to take it apart and see what I could do. All of the electronics are located on the sides of the machine, so it is necessary to take the whole thing apart to fix anything. I was momentarily stumped while trying to take the top off, but eventually got it by prying around the edges and sliding it towards the back.

It turned out to be a very easy fix -- the main power rocker switch on the side was broken. I looked around to see if I had a suitable replacement but couldn't find anything. After examining the switch some more I determined it was a momentary rocker switch. Luckily I have a ton of momentary normally-open push-buttons.

I cut up a piece of hard plastic into the correct size for the hole that the rocker switch left behind and mounted the push-button in the center. After soldering the wires back and covering them with heatshrink, it was good to go. I even reassembled the whole thing without any leftover screws (I put each set of screws into its own labeled bag to ensure I knew just where they went).

You can check out some pictures of my workspace, the insides of the machine, and my fix below. I also have a video of it successfully powering on after reassembly.
